name: Nyx
description: The starry realm in which the gods take form from mortal belief.

timeline.summary: At night Leandros asks Mnesos why the gods have abandoned them and whether they will return; Mnesos says the gods have retreated into Nyx before.
timeline.quote: The historians tell us that this is not the first time the gods have retreated into Nyx

timeline.summary: Xenocrates argues that gods are the patterns mortals recognize, personified through the power of Nyx, and that mortals are responsible for their gods; Melantha forbids it as blasphemy.
timeline.quote: Through the power of Nyx, we are responsible for our gods.

timeline.summary: In the vision the constellations of Nyx turn on Raissa's son with outrage and lightning, and he rises to meet them on a cloud of red and green power with a gleaming staff.

relations.note: The vision shows the constellation gods arrayed in outrage against her son.
relations.quote: They faced Raissa—no, they were facing her son!

pages_say.description: The night-sky realm into which the gods retreated.
The night-sky realm into which the children are said to have vanished and whose glow fades at dawn.
The night sky into which the gods have retreated.
The divine realm through whose power, Xenocrates says, mortals create their gods.
The night sky of constellation gods that Raissa sees in her final vision.
The starry realm in which the gods take form from mortal belief.
The realm of the gods of Theros; Elspeth and Ajani seek to journey into it.
